newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to cut 140,000 bags coffee exports Jan-June.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to cut 140,000 bags coffee exports Jan-June.

text.p: Brazil will cut its January to June arabica exports by 140,000 60-kg bags to comply with an agreement of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) to support robustas, a senior commodities official said.

Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department in the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, said Colombia had agreed to slash its coffee exports by 100,000 bags and Central American producers would collectively cut sales by 60,000 bags.
The cuts follow last month's ACPC meeting in Rio de Janeiro where producers agreed to slice exports in the first half of 1997 to show support for robusta producers.
ACPC member countries agreed to a 1.3 million bag cut, including 300,000 bags arabica.
"Brazil will cut exports by 140,000 bags, Colombia by 100,000 and 60,000 bags will be distributed among the Central American countries," Assis told reporters.
He said Brazil exported about 1.07 million bags of coffee in January.
Assis said no particular efforts were being made to ensure Brazilian exporters stuck to the new export limit of 5.86 million 60-kg bags in the January-June period.
"We have permanent meetings with the private sector to monitor shipments," he said. "We think we can leave taking some kind of measures (to stem sales) till later."
Assis said the distribution of arabica export cuts between producers was decided at the ACPC meeting in Rio itself.
